title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 9 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Corinthians chapter 9 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 9 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Corinthians Chapter 9.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 9, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Paul asks if he is an apostle
Paul discusses the power to eat
Paul quotes the law of Moses
questions.correctAnswer: Paul asks if he is an apostle
questions.explanation: This is the first statement made in the chapter, found in 1 Corinthians 9:1.

questions.question: What does Paul refer to as the seal of his apostleship?
options: His ability to lead a wife
questions.explanation: Paul states that the seal of his apostleship is the Corinthians themselves, as mentioned in 1 Corinthians 9:2.

questions.question: Who is mentioned alongside Paul in discussing the power to forbear working?
questions.explanation: Paul mentions Barnabas in connection with the power to forbear working in 1 Corinthians 9:6.

questions.question: What analogy does Paul use to discuss the rights of apostles?
questions.explanation: Paul compares the rights of apostles to those of a soldier who does not serve at his own charges, as found in 1 Corinthians 9:7.

questions.question: What does Paul ask about eating and drinking?
options: Have we not power to eat and drink?
questions.correctAnswer: Have we not power to eat and drink?
questions.explanation: This question is directly stated in 1 Corinthians 9:4.

questions.question: According to Paul, who should not be muzzled?
questions.explanation: Paul refers to the command not to muzzle the ox in 1 Corinthians 9:9.

questions.question: What does Paul use to defend his rights as an apostle?
questions.explanation: Paul references the law to support his argument about the rights of apostles in 1 Corinthians 9:8.

questions.question: What is one thing Paul mentions that a soldier does?
questions.explanation: Paul mentions that a soldier goes to war in 1 Corinthians 9:7.

questions.question: What does Paul question about leading a sister or wife?
options: Have we not power to lead about a sister, a wife?
questions.correctAnswer: Have we not power to lead about a sister, a wife?
questions.explanation: This question is posed in 1 Corinthians 9:5.

questions.question: To whom does Paul claim he is an apostle?
questions.explanation: Paul asserts that he is an apostle to the Corinthians in 1 Corinthians 9:2.

questions.question: Does Paul say that he is free?
questions.explanation: Paul explicitly states he is free in 1 Corinthians 9:1.

questions.question: Is it mentioned that God takes care of oxen?
questions.explanation: Paul asks if God takes care of oxen in 1 Corinthians 9:9.

questions.question: Did Paul see Jesus Christ our Lord?
questions.explanation: Paul states he has seen Jesus Christ our Lord in 1 Corinthians 9:1.

questions.question: Did Paul mention the need for apostles to have wives?
questions.explanation: Paul does not say that apostles need wives; he discusses the power to lead about a sister, a wife in 1 Corinthians 9:5, but does not imply necessity.

questions.question: Did Paul claim he has no rights as an apostle?
questions.explanation: Paul argues for his rights as an apostle throughout the chapter, and does not claim he has no rights.

medium.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 9 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Corinthians Chapter 9 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 9:10 say about those who plow and thresh?
questions.explanation: This is correct because 1 Corinthians 9:10 states that 'he that ploweth should plow in hope; and that he that thresheth in hope should be partaker of his hope.'

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 9:11 promise will happen if spiritual things are sown?
questions.explanation: This is correct as 1 Corinthians 9:11 states, 'If we have sown unto you spiritual things, is it a great thing if we shall reap your carnal things?'

questions.question: What does Paul say he suffers for in 1 Corinthians 9:12?
options: To hinder the gospel of Christ.
questions.correctAnswer: To hinder the gospel of Christ.
questions.explanation: Paul mentions in 1 Corinthians 9:12 that he has not used his power over them 'but suffer all things, lest we should hinder the gospel of Christ.'

questions.question: What connection does 1 Corinthians 9:13 have with 1 Corinthians 9:12?
options: Both discuss living from the gospel.
questions.correctAnswer: Both discuss living from the gospel.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:13 states that those who minister about holy things live from the things of the temple, connecting to the idea in 1 Corinthians 9:12 about the power to receive support.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 9:14, who has ordained that those who preach the gospel should live of the gospel?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:14 states, 'Even so hath the Lord ordained that they which preach the gospel should live of the gospel.'

questions.question: What does Paul express regarding his own actions in 1 Corinthians 9:15?
options: He prefers to die rather than hinder the gospel.
He is proud of his glory.
questions.correctAnswer: He prefers to die rather than hinder the gospel.
questions.explanation: Paul states in 1 Corinthians 9:15, 'for it were better for me to die, than that any man should make my glorying void.'

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 9:16, what does Paul say is necessary for him?
questions.explanation: Paul states in 1 Corinthians 9:16, 'for necessity is laid upon me; yea, woe is unto me, if I preach not the gospel!'

questions.question: What does Paul identify as his reward in 1 Corinthians 9:18?
options: To make the gospel of Christ without charge.
To be recognized as an apostle.
questions.correctAnswer: To make the gospel of Christ without charge.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:18 indicates that Paul's reward is to preach the gospel without charge, stating, 'that I abuse not my power in the gospel.'

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 9:1 reveal about Paul’s identity?
questions.explanation: Paul begins 1 Corinthians 9:1 by asking, 'Am I not an apostle?' which affirms his apostolic identity.

questions.question: How does Paul defend his apostleship in 1 Corinthians 9:2?
options: By pointing to the seal of his apostleship.
questions.correctAnswer: By pointing to the seal of his apostleship.
questions.explanation: In 1 Corinthians 9:2, Paul states, 'for the seal of mine apostleship are ye in the Lord,' indicating that the Corinthians are evidence of his work.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 9:7, Paul compares his work to which of the following?
questions.explanation: Paul asks, 'Who goeth a warfare any time at his own charges?' in 1 Corinthians 9:7, comparing his role to that of a soldier.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 9:9, what does the law of Moses say?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:9 refers to the law stating, 'Thou shalt not muzzle the mouth of the ox that treadeth out the corn.'

questions.question: True or False: Paul has a right to receive support for his ministry.
questions.explanation: This statement is true because Paul argues throughout 1 Corinthians 9 that those who preach the gospel have the right to receive support.

questions.question: True or False: Paul seeks to benefit personally from preaching the gospel.
questions.explanation: This statement is false as Paul emphasizes that he preaches the gospel without charge and does not seek personal gain, indicating his focus is on the gospel.

questions.question: True or False: Paul believes his apostleship is validated by the work he has done among the Corinthians.
questions.explanation: This statement is false as Paul indicates that while he is an apostle, he does not rely solely on this for validation; rather, the Corinthians themselves validate his apostleship.

hard.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 9 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Corinthians Chapter 9.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 9:19, why does Paul make himself a servant to all?
options: That he might gain the more
Because he was commanded by the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: That he might gain the more
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:19 states Paul made himself servant unto all that he might gain the more.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 9:20, how does Paul become to those without law?
options: As a strict teacher of the law
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:21 explains that Paul became as without law to those without law, but not without law to God, showing his adaptability.

questions.question: What is the ultimate purpose Paul states for being all things to all men in 1 Corinthians 9:22?
options: That he might by all means save some
questions.correctAnswer: That he might by all means save some
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:22 declares Paul is made all things to all men so that by all means he might save some.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 9:24, what analogy does Paul use to encourage believers to strive for their goal?
options: A race where only one receives the prize
questions.correctAnswer: A race where only one receives the prize
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:24 uses the analogy of runners in a race where only one wins the prize to motivate believers to run so they may obtain.

questions.question: What contrast does Paul make about the crowns in 1 Corinthians 9:25?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:25 contrasts the athletes striving for a corruptible crown with Christians aiming for an incorruptible one.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 9:27, what does Paul say he does to his body?
options: Keeps under and brings into subjection
questions.correctAnswer: Keeps under and brings into subjection
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:27 states Paul keeps under his body and brings it into subjection to avoid becoming a castaway after preaching to others.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'dunamis' in 1 Corinthians 9:12 mean?
questions.explanation: 'Dunamis' in 1 Corinthians 9:12 is commonly translated as 'power' or 'ability,' referring to the authority or strength to exercise rights.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in 1 Corinthians 9:19-23 where Paul adapts his behavior to different groups?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:19-23 uses parallelism by repeating a similar structure to describe becoming like various groups to gain them.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is echoed by Paul's argument about not muzzling the ox in 1 Corinthians 9:9?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:9 cites the law 'Thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treadeth out the corn,' which comes from Deuteronomy 25:4.

questions.question: The theme of running a race to obtain a prize in 1 Corinthians 9:24-25 is also reflected in which New Testament passage?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:1 also uses the metaphor of running a race with endurance, echoing the theme in 1 Corinthians 9:24-25.

questions.question: What verse directly precedes 1 Corinthians 9:19, which begins the section on becoming all things to all men?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:18 concludes the previous thought before Paul begins in 9:19 about being free yet making himself servant.

questions.question: In the historical context of 1 Corinthians 9, what cultural practice is Paul referring to when mentioning 'leading about a sister, a wife' in verse 5?
options: Right of apostles to be accompanied by a believing wife
Marriage customs forbidding women to travel
questions.correctAnswer: Right of apostles to be accompanied by a believing wife
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:5 references the cultural and apostolic right to have a believing wife travel with them, indicating support and legitimacy.

questions.question: What typology is Paul employing in 1 Corinthians 9:24-27 when comparing Christian discipline to athletic competition?
options: Christian life as a disciplined race
questions.correctAnswer: Christian life as a disciplined race
questions.explanation: Paul uses the typology of athletic competition to represent the Christian life as one requiring discipline and striving for an incorruptible prize (1 Corinthians 9:24-27).

questions.question: How does Paul's use of the phrase 'lest I myself should be a castaway' in 1 Corinthians 9:27 reflect a literary inclusio within the chapter?
options: It bookends the chapter emphasizing personal accountability
It introduces a new theme unrelated to the chapter
It repeats the first verse verbatim
It quotes an Old Testament law
questions.correctAnswer: It bookends the chapter emphasizing personal accountability
questions.explanation: The phrase in 1 Corinthians 9:27 forms a literary inclusio with the opening verses, highlighting Paul's concern for his own standing after preaching.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Corinthians 9:14, the Lord ordained that those who preach the gospel should live of the gospel.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:14 states explicitly that the Lord ordained that those preaching the gospel should live of the gospel.

theological.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 9 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Corinthians Chapter 9 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Corinthians 9:14 teach about the provision for those who preach the gospel?
options: The Lord ordained that those who preach the gospel should live of the gospel
Preachers must work secular jobs to support themselves
Gospel ministers should rely solely on voluntary offerings
Those who preach must not expect any material support
questions.correctAnswer: The Lord ordained that those who preach the gospel should live of the gospel
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:14 explicitly states that the Lord ordained that those who preach the gospel should live of the gospel, indicating divine provision for ministers.

questions.question: What doctrine about apostolic authority and freedom is taught in 1 Corinthians 9:1?
options: An apostle is recognized by seeing Jesus Christ and by the work done in the Lord
Apostles must be appointed by church elders only
Apostolic authority depends on performing miracles
Apostles are servants without any personal freedom
questions.correctAnswer: An apostle is recognized by seeing Jesus Christ and by the work done in the Lord
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:1 emphasizes that Paul's apostleship is evidenced by having seen the Lord Jesus and by the believers being his work in the Lord, affirming his authority and freedom.

questions.question: What doctrine about self-discipline and sanctification is found in 1 Corinthians 9:27?
options: Believers must exercise rigorous self-control to avoid being disqualified
Sanctification is automatic for all who preach the gospel
Human effort is irrelevant to one's standing before God
Physical discipline is unnecessary for spiritual growth
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must exercise rigorous self-control to avoid being disqualified
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:27 shows that Paul disciplines his body to bring it into subjection, lest after preaching to others he himself should be disqualified, teaching the necessity of self-control in sanctification.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 Corinthians 9:10 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:10 discusses God’s care for oxen and human laborers, illustrating God's providence in providing for those who work.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 Corinthians 9:16 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Verse 16 states that Paul has a necessity laid upon him to preach the gospel, reflecting the divine compulsion or necessity in his commission.

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 9:19–23 prepare for the biblical theme of incarnation and identification with humanity?
options: Paul becomes all things to all men to save some, reflecting Christ's incarnation
Paul emphasizes separation from worldly people to maintain holiness
Paul refuses to adapt to cultural contexts to preserve gospel purity
Paul only preaches to Jews to maintain covenant exclusivity
questions.correctAnswer: Paul becomes all things to all men to save some, reflecting Christ's incarnation
questions.explanation: Paul’s self-identification with various groups to win them mirrors Christ’s incarnation to identify with humanity (Philippians 2:7), preparing this redemptive theme.

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 9:24–27 connect to the broader biblical narrative about perseverance in faith?
options: It calls for disciplined endurance to obtain the incorruptible crown, echoing Hebrews’ teaching on perseverance
It encourages believers to rely solely on grace without effort
It promotes a casual approach to faith as a guarantee of salvation
It rejects the metaphor of athletic competition as unspiritual
questions.correctAnswer: It calls for disciplined endurance to obtain the incorruptible crown, echoing Hebrews’ teaching on perseverance
questions.explanation: The athletic imagery of running and fighting to win the incorruptible crown aligns with Hebrews’ emphasis on enduring faith to receive the eternal reward.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 9 and 10 teach about God's care and the principle of just reward?
options: God cares for laborers and expects them to share in the fruits of their work
God only cares for animals, not humans
Justice requires laborers to forfeit their rewards for the benefit of others
God’s law is irrelevant to Christian ministry
questions.correctAnswer: God cares for laborers and expects them to share in the fruits of their work
questions.explanation: Verses 9 and 10 cite the law about not muzzling an ox and interpret it as God’s provision for those who labor, teaching just reward for work.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 12 and 13 teach about gospel ministry and rights?
options: Those who minister in the gospel have a right to material support, though Paul chose not to exercise this right
Gospel ministers must not expect any earthly support
Material support is a sign of spiritual failure
Only Old Testament priests have rights to material provisions
questions.correctAnswer: Those who minister in the gospel have a right to material support, though Paul chose not to exercise this right
questions.explanation: Verses 12 and 13 affirm that gospel ministers have rights to support, but Paul refrained from using them to avoid hindering the gospel.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 18 and 19 teach about the motives and methods of gospel ministry?
options: Paul preaches without charge to avoid abusing power, demonstrating servant leadership
Paul charges fees for preaching to maintain his ministry
Paul uses power to compel belief
Paul’s freedom excludes any obligation to others
questions.correctAnswer: Paul preaches without charge to avoid abusing power, demonstrating servant leadership
questions.explanation: Verses 18 and 19 explain Paul’s choice to preach free of charge so as not to abuse his apostolic power and to serve others selflessly.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that 1 Corinthians 9:6–7 teaches that apostles selfishly demand material support. What does the passage actually teach?
options: Apostles have the right to material support but may choose to forbear it
Apostles must always demand material support
Material support is never permitted for apostles
Apostles should reject material support to appear humble
questions.correctAnswer: Apostles have the right to material support but may choose to forbear it
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:6–7 affirms apostles’ rights to material support but Paul and Barnabas chose to forbear working to not hinder the gospel.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Corinthians 9:4 teach about the rights of Christian ministers?
options: Christian ministers have rights to basic necessities like food and drink
Ministers must live in poverty by necessity
Ministers should not expect any rights from the church
Ministers’ rights override the needs of the church
questions.correctAnswer: Christian ministers have rights to basic necessities like food and drink
questions.explanation: Verse 4 poses rhetorical questions affirming that ministers have rights to eat and drink, underscoring their entitlement to basic provision.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 Corinthians 9:17 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Paul states that whether he preaches willingly or unwillingly, the gospel dispensation is committed to him, highlighting God's sovereign purpose.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 20 and 21 teach about contextualization and gospel mission?
options: Paul adapts to various cultural and legal statuses to effectively reach diverse groups while remaining under Christ's law
Paul rejects any cultural adaptation to maintain Jewish purity
Paul compromises the gospel message to please different groups
Salvation depends on observing the law strictly
questions.correctAnswer: Paul adapts to various cultural and legal statuses to effectively reach diverse groups while remaining under Christ's law
questions.explanation: Verses 20 and 21 show Paul’s flexible approach to evangelism, adapting culturally without compromising his submission to Christ's law.

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 9:15 connect to the theme of apostolic humility and suffering elsewhere in Scripture?
options: Paul prefers death over losing the validity of his gospel boasting, exemplifying apostolic suffering
Paul boasts of his rights and privileges as an apostle
Paul seeks honor and glory above all
Paul avoids suffering by all means
questions.correctAnswer: Paul prefers death over losing the validity of his gospel boasting, exemplifying apostolic suffering
questions.explanation: Verse 15 expresses Paul's willingness to suffer death rather than have his gospel boasting nullified, paralleling Christ’s passion and apostolic humility.
